items.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023
items.q: So often on the recordings that I’ve made I’ll have something in mind and then somebody like Phil Woods will come along and just change the entire direction of what I imagined, and it’s Phil Woods, well of course.

ctx.x: No. John Ellis, who played clarinet, I’ve been recording and playing gigs with him, I don’t know maybe for ten years now. And he’s got this real fresh open sound. And that was overdubbed, I mean we had that track and then you’re absolutely right to say that whole track is built on that ghost note. And the lyrics — “Too many people/Got nothing to say/It’s underhanded but I can understand it.” It was just play. It was fun. And I gave a copy of that track to Ellis. Because he had worked — I mean it was kind of an…

people. If I like somebody’s approach and I like them as a player I’m open to what they come up with that is probably more interesting than what I’m looking for. Because what I’m looking for is just one — there’s no right part really, to me. You know a lot of things could work. So often on the recordings that I’ve made I’ll have something in mind and then somebody like Phil Woods will come along and just change the entire direction of what I imagined, and it’s Phil Woods, well of course. You know that’s why he’s…
Yeah and the bass clarinet doubling the bass parts, very cool.
